subject: Is there any option to use fixed factor method when cp = "fa"?

messages.author: 4d78542ee90d0285
messages.subject: Is there any option to use fixed factor method when cp = "fa"?
parts:
Hello Dr. Merkle, 

First of all, thanks for all the work you put on this project, this is an amazing package and I'm learning a lot by running models and simulations. I have a very specific question, is there any option to use fixed factor method of identification when cp = "fa"? 

I'll appreciate any help you can give me.

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Is there any option to use fixed factor method when cp = "fa"?
parts:
Esteban,

Do you mean to fix the factor variance to 1, instead of a factor loading? If so, then it seems like you want the argument std.lv=TRUE.

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Is there any option to use fixed factor method when cp = "fa"?
parts:
Thanks for you quick reply. I know about the argument std.lv = TRUE but when I try to use it when cp = "fa" , I get the following message:

Error in blavaan(mod, data, std.lv = T, orthogonal = F, group = "group",  : 
  blavaan ERROR: 'fa' prior strategy cannot be used with std.lv=TRUE.

This is my simulated example:

pop.CFA.A1 <- '
  f1 =~ c(.7,.68)*x1 +
         c(.7,.7)*x2 +
        c(.7,.7)*x3 
  f2 =~ c(.7,.7)*x4 +
         c(.7,.7)*x5+
         c(.7,.7)*x6  

  f1 ~~ c(.3, .3)*f2

  x1 ~~ c(.51,.32)*x1
  x2 ~~ c(.51,.51)*x2
  x3 ~~ c(.51,.51)*x3
  x4 ~~ c(.51,.51)*x4
  x5 ~~ c(.51,.51)*x5
  x6 ~~ c(.51,.51)*x6

  f1 ~~ c(1,1)*f1
  f2 ~~ c(1,1)*f2

  x1 ~ c(0,.02)*1 
  x2 ~ c(0,0)*1 
  x3 ~ c(0,0)*1 
  x4 ~ c(0,0)*1 
  x5 ~ c(0,0)*1 
  x6 ~ c(0,0)*1 
  '
data <- simulateData(pop.CFA.A1,
               meanstructure = TRUE, sample.nobs = c(500, 500))



mod <- '
 f1 =~ x1 +
       x2 +
       x3 
  f2 =~ x4 +
        x5+
        x6
'



bfit  <- bcfa(mod, data, std.lv = T, orthogonal=F,
adapt = adp, burnin = brn, cp="fa", group = "group",
sample = 5000)


Is this happening because it is multigroup model?

Thanks again for your help.

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Is there any option to use fixed factor method when cp = "fa"?
parts:
Sorry, it has been awhile since I looked at that part of the code. That error is there because, under the "fa" strategy, extra parameters get added to the model that make it difficult to fix the latent variance at 1 (because the latent variance becomes a function of multiple parameters).

It might be possible to do this, but it is lower priority for me because I generally think the "srs" strategy is preferable. So, unless you have a reason against it, I would say to use std.lv=TRUE under the srs strategy.

Ed
